title: Rustic Works — order-routing telemetry & deploy triage
content:
Call summary (2025-02-10):
Attendees: Tom Gallagher (Rustic Works, CTO), Ana Morales (Rustic Works, Eng Lead), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Evan Chen (Redwood Infra), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SRE)
Agenda: stabilize order-routing latency, telemetry gaps, private deployment checklist, canary strategy for model/routing changes.

Customer context / goals:
- Rustic Works runs a real-time fulfillment router that decides which warehouse to route orders to based on product, inventory signals, carrier ETA and a learned policy.
- Target QPS: 120–250 requests/s during peak; typical request size ~ 80 tokens of prompt + 1–3 short structured fields.
- SLO: p95 < 150ms, p99 < 300ms end-to-end for decision latency.
- Must run in their VPC (GovCloud-like controls) with customer KMS and audit logs forwarded to their Splunk instance.

Key technical notes from call:
- Current prototype uses hosted Redwood API with a small instruction-tuned reranker + cached embedding lookup for candidate pruning. They saw occasional rank inversions after switching to the q4_0 quantized variant.
- Telemetry gaps: they do not have per-route token breakdowns; only see total request time. Need token-level cost/latency traces to correlate spikes with KV-cache misses.
- KV/prefix caching behavior: they build cache keys that include shipping_zone + sku_prefix. Observed stale routing recommendations when cache TTL is 10m — leads to incorrect routing during inventory churn. Suggested setting TTL ~ 30–90s for hot SKUs, with selective longer TTLs for stable SKUs.
- Batching/backpressure gotcha: when the router autoscaler spins up new workers during surge, batching windows increase (to fill batches) and occasional requests hit timeout (gateway-level 350ms). Need adaptive batch-window config that respects latency SLO and can temporarily disable batching for canary routes.
- Tokenization gotcha: order reference strings sometimes include non-ascii chars (vendor-specific prefixes) that the tokenizer splits into many tokens; this inflates token counts and unpredictably increases cost/latency. Recommend pre-normalization on client side (strip/control chars, map vendor prefixes) + server-side validation.
- Embedding mismatch: their similarity index was built with 512-d vectors but the candidate model they plan to use outputs 768-d vectors after a model swap. This breaks nearest-neighbor tables and causes silent failures. Action: freeze embedding dimensionality or schedule reindexing as part of the model rollout.
- Security: customer insists on mutual TLS to the private control plane and HSM-backed key usage for model artifacts. Need to confirm our private agent supports client cert auth for the control plane endpoints.

Observed anomalies during demo runs:
- During a 1-hour soak test (peak sim), p50 stable but p99 spikes mapped to a single worker node that had lower GPU util and elevated kernel retries — suspected kernel selection regressions in quantized path.
- Caching metric: cache hit-rate reported 78% overall, but top-100 SKUs have 96% while long-tail SKUs are ~32% — candidate for adaptive TTL + frequency-based tiering.

Requirements (from Rustic Works):
- Production-grade private deployment in their AWS account, with VPC peering, private control plane, and KMS-managed model keys.
- Canaries by route: must be able to roll out model/routing changes only for 3% of traffic for a given route (not globally).
- Per-request trace id that they can correlate to their Kafka event stream; trace id must appear in our logs and exported telemetry.
- Ability to pin model variant per route and automatically fall back to a cheaper variant on capacity constraints.

Short-term recommended mitigations (during private deploy prep):
- Lower default KV cache TTL to 90s for inventory-sensitive routes; implement hot-key fast-path with TTL 15–45s.
- Add pre-tokenization sanitizers to the client SDK (strip non-printables; vendor-prefix map).
- Disable batching for canary traffic and routes with SLA < 200ms. Add an adaptive batch-window config flag.
- Lock embedding dimension via config and add a preflight reindex job that must succeed before switching model index.
- Add a lightweight telemetry shim in their account to surface token-level breakdowns (sample 1% requests initially).

Longer-term product asks from Rustic Works (they will push):
- Route-aware cost forecasting: show expected unit cost delta for a route if they switch to a different quantized variant.
- Per-route error regression alerts tied to deployment changes + automatic rollback hooks.
- Native connector for their internal order DB to seed prompt caches (secure read-only pull).

Action items / owners / dates:
- Evan: prototype adaptive batch-window flag and force-disable-for-canary logic (due 2025-02-20).
- Priya: open RFC for KV-TTL tiering + hot-key fast-path + sample config (RINF-2345) (due 2025-02-14).
- Sofia: verify private control plane mutual-TLS support and KMS HSM integration checklist; schedule infra runbook (due 2025-02-18).
- Jessica (sales): draft contract addendum for VPC + KMS requirements and updated SLAs (due 2025-02-21).
- Rustic Works (Ana): share example order records (anonymized) and their embedding index metadata (due 2025-02-13).

Open questions / follow-ups needed from customer:
- Are long-tail SKUs expected to have predictable churn windows (e.g., daily/weekly)? If yes, we can do TTL seasonality.
- Confirm acceptable fallback policy if the pinned model is out of capacity (route-level fallback to cheaper quantized variant vs global fallback).
- Do they have an internal reindex window for embeddings or will they rely on live reindexing?

Notes to self / SE heuristics learned here:
- For order-routing, small token counts hide big UX issues: a single vendor prefix or special char can blow up tokens. Always push pre-normalization as best practice.
- Adaptive batching should be first-class per-route opt: policy = {min_latency_SLO, max_batch_size, warmup_samples}.
- Quantized model regressions often show up as subtle rank shifts — include a small held-out ranking task in canary checks.

Next meeting: follow-up tech deep-dive with Rustic Works mapping canary wiring + telemetry export (proposed 2025-02-24).

Quick links & refs: RINF-2345 (KV TTL RFC), PR #672 (routing/service changes), slack thread above for demo logs.

Scratch brain dump (raw):
- think about a dynamic ttl service that ingests SKU churn metrics and emits TTL overrides via small policy file in S3 (signed).
- reindex job can be a k8s job controlled by their pipeline (will need IAM role).
- consider adding a per-route "no-batch" header so client can explicitly opt-out on latency-critical calls.

~ end of notes
